Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which award did Knut Korsæth receive?
Document 1: Title: The Honorable Knut Korsæth: A Life of Dedicated Service

In the realm of Norwegian politics, few individuals have left an indelible mark on the nation's history as Knut Korsæth, a stalwart politician who dedicated his life to serving the people of Norway. Among the many accolades he received for his tireless efforts, one stands out as a testament to his unwavering commitment: the prestigious Commander of the Order of St. Olav‎. The Order of St. Olav‎, established in 1847, is Norway's highest honor, bestowed upon individuals who have made significant contributions to the country's welfare, culture, and society. To be recognized with this esteemed award is a rare distinction, reserved for those who have demonstrated exceptional dedication, leadership, and service to the nation. Knut Korsæth's journey to receiving this honor began early in his life, as he embarked on a path of public service that would span decades. Born and raised in Norway, Korsæth was instilled with a strong sense of duty and responsibility, which drove him to pursue a career in politics. He quickly rose through the ranks, earning the respect and admiration of his peers and constituents alike. Throughout his political career, Korsæth demonstrated a deep understanding of the needs of the Norwegian people, working tirelessly to address the challenges facing the nation. He was a vocal advocate for social justice, education, and economic development, using his platform to champion the causes that mattered most to his fellow citizens. One of Korsæth's most notable achievements was his instrumental role in shaping Norway's post-war reconstruction efforts. In the aftermath of World War II, the country faced significant challenges in rebuilding its infrastructure, economy, and social fabric. Korsæth played a key role in developing and implementing policies that helped Norway recover and thrive, earning him widespread recognition and admiration. As his reputation grew, so did his influence. Korsæth became a respected leader within his party and a trusted advisor to successive governments. His wisdom, integrity, and commitment to the well-being of the Norwegian people earned him the respect of his political opponents, who often sought his counsel and collaboration. In recognition of his outstanding contributions to Norway, King Olav V, the monarch at the time, bestowed upon Korsæth the Commander of the Order of St. Olav‎.
Document 2: **Norwegian Politician Knut Korsæth Honored with Prestigious French Award**

Oslo, Norway - In a ceremony held at the French Embassy in Oslo yesterday, Norwegian politician Knut Korsæth was bestowed the esteemed title of Commander of the Legion of Honour, the third highest rank in the French Legion of Honour. This prestigious award recognizes Korsæth's outstanding contributions to strengthening Franco-Norwegian relations and his tireless efforts in promoting cultural exchange between the two nations. The ceremony, attended by dignitaries from both countries, was presided over by French Ambassador to Norway, Monsieur Pierre Dupont. In his address, Dupont praised Korsæth's dedication to fostering a deeper understanding between France and Norway, citing his instrumental role in establishing the Norway-France Cultural Exchange Program in 2015. "Knut Korsæth is a true champion of international cooperation and a shining example of the power of diplomacy," Dupont said. "His commitment to promoting mutual understanding and respect between our nations is truly deserving of this highest honor." Korsæth, a member of the Norwegian Parliament since 2009, has been a vocal advocate for strengthening ties between Norway and France. His efforts have led to increased collaboration in areas such as education, trade, and environmental protection. "I am deeply humbled and grateful to receive this prestigious award," Korsæth said in an exclusive interview with our newspaper. "It is a testament to the hard work and dedication of countless individuals who have worked alongside me to build bridges between our nations. I am proud to have played a part in fostering a stronger relationship between Norway and France." According to data from the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, bilateral trade between Norway and France has increased by 25% since 2015, with cultural exchange programs experiencing a 50% surge in participation during the same period. Korsæth's award is seen as a significant milestone in the history of Franco-Norwegian relations, marking a new era of cooperation and collaboration between the two nations. "Knut Korsæth's recognition is a reflection of the strong bond between our countries," said Norwegian Prime Minister, Erna Solberg. "We are proud to have him as a representative of Norway on the international stage." As Commander of the Legion of Honour, Korsæth joins an esteemed group of individuals who have made significant contributions to French culture and international relations.
